sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Bibliographic only: five refs, none descriptive. meds = 'a wordlist or less' for both Clouse 1992 (SIL Papua wordlist ms., 'a couple of hundred words') and Jones 1987 (unpublished SIL Papua survey report, 10 pp., covering Nisa-Anasi, Barapasi, Sauri, Tefaro, Demisa, Burate, Kofei, Tunggare, Woria, Awera, Rasawa, Saponi, Warembori). No grammar, phonology or sketch exists.

sources.citation: Sister-language check Tunggare/Wate [tung1293] (Maturbongs 2023 Frasa Bahasa Wate; Voorhoeve 1975 PL B-31 and PL C-38; Wate Living Dictionary; Laura Arnold project pages)
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing on stress for the mutually intelligible sister variety either; Maturbongs 2023 p.16 says Wate grammar has not been studied; Arnold's Wate documentation (Firebird grant, March 2026) is in progress and unpublished.

sources.citation: Kamholz, David. 2012. The Keuw isolate: Preliminary materials and classification. Language & Linguistics in Melanesia, Special Issue 2012 Part I, 243-268.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing on Burate phonology. p.243: Burate (bti, East Geelvink Bay) live downstream near the mouth of the Poronai, village Totoberi. p.252: 'Speakers of Keuw and Burate claim that there is no resemblance between the two languages. A cursory comparison of Keuw with Wate/Tarunggare (trt), which is mutually intelligible with Burate, confirms this' followed by a 16-item Wate list (author's field notes, no stress marks). p.249: Keuw name derived from Burate kebete 'tree person'.
